# What each check cannot see, point by point

*Generated by `python tools/kernel_table.py` from `tests/kernel_boundaries.py`; `tests/test_kernel.py` holds every row and refuses a document that has drifted from the catalogue. Do not edit by hand.*

Every check in the machine is invariant under some transformation of what it reads: change the reply, the document, or the record that way and the verdict does not move. That set is the check's kernel, the class of things it cannot do. A general statement of the class would be a conjecture; what can be stated exactly is a boundary point: one transformation the verdict moves under, as small as it can be made, beside one it does not, as close to the first as it can be brought. Each row below is such a point, and each is asserted both ways by the suite: the moved verdict differs from the base, the unmoved one equals it. A row whose first column is empty names a check that nothing moves.

The rows are read against a survival. A reply that passed every check passed exactly these checks, with exactly these blind spots, on these records; the machine never promotes, and this table is the reason stated in full. A point that begins to fail because a check now sees what the row says it cannot is the boundary moving, and the row is rewritten in the same change.

Two rows were written as boundaries and then decided to be defects, on the committed records: P-02 (nine cycle replies were scored on a quoted draft rather than the corrected answer that followed it, H40) and G-08 (the containment check did not normalise whitespace where the occurrence check did, H41); each row now states the boundary after the change, and its note says what moved. One row records a boundary that is arguably a defect and is kept until decided: V-01 (a closed-list item is found on a page by substring). P-07 records a limit kept deliberately.

| Point | Check | The verdict moves under | The verdict is unchanged under | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-01 | Schema: pattern | a date written outside the pattern (`13/10/2025`) | a string that fits the pattern and is no date (`2025-13-45`) | the leave-request fields carry the `unknown` oracle, so the field verdict is the schema check alone |
| S-02 | Schema: enumeration | a listed value in another case (`Annual`) | another listed value the document does not support (`sick`) |  |
| S-03 | Schema: maxLength | one character over the bound (161 of 160) | a string exactly at the bound with no meaning (160 times `x`) |  |
| S-04 | Schema: integer type | the number as a string (`"5"`), or JSON `true` where an integer is due | an integer of any size or sign (`5000`, `-5`) |  |
| S-05 | Schema: boolean type | the word as a string (`"true"`), or `1` for `true` | the other truth value (`false` where the document says the manager was told) |  |
| S-06 | Schema: closed key set | one key the form does not define (`EXTRA_FIELD`) | the same keys in another order |  |
| O-01 | `exact` oracle | a second space inside the value (`Alice  Nguyen`), or a change of case | any change to another field of the same reply | the span check normalises whitespace (G-01); the oracle does not |
| O-02 | `exact` oracle on a number | the next integer (`196641`) | nothing on the field; the float `196640.0` is refused before any oracle runs (P-04) |  |
| O-03 | `any_of` oracle | a value outside the admitted readings (`Warehouse B Dock 3`, no comma) | which admitted reading was taken (`warehouse B, Dock 3`) |  |
| O-04 | `regex` oracle | a summary without the required word (`hurt his arm`) | a summary that contains the word and says the opposite (`No injury to the wrist`) |  |
| O-05 | `unknown` oracle |  | any value at all (`Nobody` for the employee's name) |  |
| O-06 | `absent` oracle | the key present with any value, `null` included (`UNEXPECTED_PRESENT`) | any change to another field | a present `null` is a present key |
| O-07 | Expected abstention (`any_of` holding `null`) | a value where the document gives none (`2025-05-27`) | why the field is null: with a span quoting an unrelated sentence, or with no span at all | the span is judged by the grounding check, not by the oracle |
| P-01 | JSON recovery | prose or a code fence around the object (`recovered_from_prose` becomes true) | blank lines and indentation around a bare object |  |
| P-02 | JSON recovery: which object | the position of the objects: the last top-level object is scored, and the last fenced one when any fence holds an object | the key counts: a larger draft before a smaller final answer, and a smaller draft before a larger one, both score the last | H40: until 9 September the object with the most keys was scored, and nine cycle replies that dropped a criticised key were read on the draft that still carried it |
| P-06 | JSON recovery: fences | a fence around an earlier object: the fenced object is scored over a later bare one | a bare object after the last fenced one |  |
| P-07 | JSON recovery: an unparsable final object |  | a final object refused for a float (`{"a": 1.5}`), or one that does not close: the earlier draft that parsed is scored | recorded, not changed: the reply is scored on a draft, and its recovery detail says an object was recovered from prose |
| P-03 | JSON recovery: repeated key | the order of the two values (the last wins) | which of the two the model meant |  |
| P-04 | Strict JSON | a float for an integer value (`5.0` is refused as `INVALID_JSON`) | pretty-printing, key order, and escaped characters |  |
| P-05 | An array reply | one stray character before the array: `[{…}]` is `NOT_AN_OBJECT`, `x [{…}]` recovers the object inside | how many objects the array holds |  |
| R-01 | Refusal heuristic | a listed phrase in any case, with straight or typographic apostrophes (`I’m sorry`) | a refusal in words the list does not hold (`I decline to do this.`), which is `INVALID_JSON` like any other prose |  |
| R-02 | Refusal beside a form | a listed phrase in prose around a recovered object (`I cannot stress how clear this is:`), which raises `REFUSAL_SUSPECTED` | prose without a listed phrase around the same object | the check fires on a non-refusal that contains a listed phrase; the flag is a criticism to read, not a verdict |
| G-01 | Span occurrence | one letter inside the quotation (`family weding`) | runs of spaces or a line break inside the quotation (`family   wedding`) |  |
| G-02 | Span occurrence: which sentence | a quotation that is not in the document (`wedding in Sydney`) | a quotation of an unrelated sentence that is (`Hi,` as the source of the reason) |  |
| G-03 | Span occurrence: length | an empty or blank quotation (`SPAN_MISSING`) | a one-character quotation that occurs anywhere (`.`) |  |
| G-04 | Span occurrence: case | case, when no relaxation is configured (`maya patel`) | case, under `case_insensitive`; the record names the relaxation, the verdict does not move |  |
| G-05 | Span occurrence: date ranges | a date inside the range that is not an endpoint (`25 June 2025`) | whether an endpoint was quoted or completed from the range (`24 June 2025` from `24 to 26 June 2025`); the record says which |  |
| G-06 | Value in span | a quotation that does not contain the value (`VALUE_NOT_IN_SPAN`) | a quotation that contains the value by coincidence: `Adelaide` as the employee's name, quoted from `for a family wedding in Adelaide` |  |
| G-08 | Value in span: whitespace | one letter less in the quotation (`Maya Pate`, which occurs, and no longer contains the value) | a line break or a run of spaces inside the quoted name (`Maya   Patel`) | H41: until 9 September the containment check did not normalise whitespace where the occurrence check did; no committed record carries a VALUE_NOT_IN_SPAN verdict |
| G-07 | Value in span: fields not configured | a quotation absent from the document (`sick leave`) | a value the quotation does not support, on a field outside `value_in_span_fields` (`sick` quoted from `annual leave`) |  |
| C-01 | Change against the baseline | one form field's value | a companion span key, or a key outside the form (H12) |  |
| C-02 | Change against the baseline: size |  | the size and direction of a change: one cent and everything are both `changed` |  |
| C-03 | Change against the baseline: agreement | a reply that differs from a baseline that was wrong | a reply wrong in exactly the way the baseline was wrong: two identical errors are `unchanged` |  |
| C-04 | Change against the baseline: arrays | the order of an array's items (`changed_vs_baseline` compares canonical bytes) | nothing about arrays: the same items in the same order | the `dependence` table reads the same records the other way (D-01) |
| D-01 | `dependence` table: arrays | a different item | the order of the items, counted apart as `reordered_only` | `_reordered_fields` names the field the order changed on |
| Q-01 | `field_value` predicate | case or type of the value (`melbourne`, compared as canonical JSON) | which of the listed values matched (`["Melbourne", "Sydney"]`) |  |
| Q-02 | Transport kind | a refused connection (`ConnectionRefusedError`), which is `other` | the difference between the remote end closing and resetting the connection (`RemoteDisconnected`, `ConnectionResetError`): both `disconnected` |  |
| Q-03 | Transport kind: timeouts | an HTTP status whose body says the gateway timed out (`HTTPError: status 504`), which is `http_status` | which layer timed out on the client side (`TimeoutError`, or a URLError that says `timed out`): both `timeout` | the status is read first; a body that says `timed out` under a status is the server's report, not the client's timeout |
| Q-04 | Floor class: structural `none` |  | why a refutation is `none`: a condition a repeat could never satisfy (a NEGATION reply identical to its baseline) and one it could (a wrong destination on the baseline, right on both repeats) carry the same class | the class is read with the condition in hand; H39 |
| Q-05 | Floor class: size |  | how many repeats the floor holds: `all` over one other repeat (a repeat of TRV-001) and over two (the baseline of TRV-002) is one label |  |
| U-01 | Unit splitting | a heading line at a configured level (`## Appendix`) | a bold line standing as a heading (`**Lemma 4.**`), which joins the unit before it | the third value is the bold document's count plus one, so equality says the bold line made no unit |
| U-02 | Unit splitting: fences | a heading line at a configured level | a heading line inside a fenced code block |  |
| U-03 | Unit relation `self` | the case of the heading in the claim (`the recursion lemma` no longer names the unit) | words around the heading in the claim (`the Recursion Lemma (below)`) | the relation is a case-sensitive substring test of the heading against the preamble |
| U-04 | Unit relation `declared` | a definition given as an `\iff` display: without it the Definitions unit is `other` | a definition given in prose (`is defined as`, `means`): neither is read as defining | a term's first occurrence and its heading also define it; K-BETA first occurs in the claim's own unit, so its prose definition elsewhere counts for nothing |
| U-05 | Unit relation: terms | the term in the later unit's heading (`### Lemma 4 (K-GAMMA)`) | a dependency stated by name (`by Lemma 4`), or by a term the claim's unit uses first: the lemma stays `other` | a term's first occurrence defines it, so a unit after the claim's unit is `declared` only through its heading or an `\iff` display |
| U-06 | Unit removal |  | references to the removed unit left in the rest of the document (`See the Recursion Lemma.`) |  |
| V-01 | Controls: vocabulary on the page | a page that holds none of the list | whether an item stands on its own or inside a longer item: `K-A` is on a page that holds only `K-ALPHA` | a substring test, kept: on the committed controls records every renamed-vocabulary row is the same under a longest-match rule and under a word-boundary rule, so nothing recorded supports a change |
| V-02 | Controls: the negated claim | the verdict reversing between `follows` and `does_not_follow` | a verdict moving to any third value (`insufficient`, `unknown`): counted as not followed, exactly as an unmoved verdict is | the table cannot tell a model that hedged on the negation from one that ignored it |
| K-01 | Records directory | a file that is not a record (`notes.txt`) | records of different pilots in one directory: nothing binds a directory to a pilot |  |
| K-02 | A reply beside its replay | a version 3 replay beside the reply it names in `replayed_from` (refused) | a version 2 re-score beside its original, which names no source (accepted and counted twice) | H38; the derivations pair in this tree is such a case |
| K-04 | Replay of a cycle chain | a step whose request has no recorded reply (here, the recorded replies of one chain removed): the step and those after it are `PREREQUISITE_UNAVAILABLE`, the rest of the run re-scores | the run record's absence from the replay directory: a replay reads the observations alone | H40: a re-score that reads a step's output differently from the recorded run changes the next step's request, which was never sent; a request identical to another recorded one is answered by that recorded reply and the record names it in `replayed_from` (H31) |
| K-03 | Citation check | an id that names no record | an id that names a record the sentence is not about |  |
| L-01 | Routing | no criticism at all (no live locus) | which field is wrong and how: a wrong name and a wrong site route to the same loci |  |
| L-02 | Routing: a negation answered like the baseline | a reply that differs from the baseline (TEST becomes live) | a baseline that was itself wrong: two identical wrong replies keep TEST out of the loci | `IDENTICAL_TO_BASELINE` subsumes every mismatch of a NEGATION variant |
| A-01 | Appraisal standing | one argument with readiness `UNKNOWN` supporting the reading (usable becomes contested) | an argument with readiness `PASS` supporting it: a reading nobody has argued about and one argued and passed stand alike | absence of argument is not endorsement; the label cannot tell them apart |
| A-02 | Appraisal labels | an attack from an argument labelled `in` | what the arguments say: two contradictory statements, both `PASS` and unattacked, are both `in` |  |

56 points. A survival is a survival of exactly these checks, with exactly these blind spots, on these records.
